what: Every octave-decision candidate tried for octave-v1 (Job O, Oct 12 2026), with the label-free development numbers that selected / rejected it. No human count of the 76 / 150 real scenes was read.

data.synthetic_A: 300 fresh renders, seeds 990000-990299, cnn/synth.py v2 generator as shipped (realistic weave / colour / glare / blur / shadow / resolution mix, down to 2.6 px per yarn)
data.synthetic_B: 300 fresh renders, seeds 991000-991299, same generator with extra weaves 'oxford' (ends work in pairs) and 'oxfordw' (picks in pairs) and more basket 2/2 (gen_synth.py) - structures whose visible repeat holds two yarns
data.synthetic_C: 150 fresh renders, seeds 992000-992149, plain / 2-1 / 2-2 twill with warp/weft density ratio 1.6-2.4 (poplin-like, gen_poplin.py); used as a check after the rule family was chosen
data.legacy13: 13 legacy crops with 2019 hand counts (methods/legacy.py rectification; frozen ours scores 9.23 % MAPE in this pipeline)
data.real_consistency: 150 real crops, label-free: reshoot = 41 same-patch pairs of scene reps (paper/tables/fabric_groups_v2.json), res = 47 quarter-resolution copies vs rep, rot = 51 rotated copies vs rep, copy = 27 png/byte/notebook copies vs rep; a 2x disagreement is an axis with count ratio in [1.70, 2.35] (consist.py)
data.metric_synthetic: MAPE over all axes (%), w10 = share of axes within 10 %, half / dbl = axes read at about 0.5x / 2x, fixed / broken = changed axes that went wrong->right / right->wrong

candidates.name: lattice self-similarity (spectral half-shift symmetry)
candidates.rule: R(s) = sum_k E_k cos(2 pi k.s) / sum_k E_k over the background-normalised power spectrum (components informative for the shift s); double an axis if the image is self-similar under a half-period shift (t/2, t/2 +- other period, centred (t1+t2)/2 for both axes), halve if not self-similar under the counted period; iterative
candidates.verdict: rejected: perfect separation of true vs half hypotheses on legacy13 but many false doublings on synthetic yarn profiles and more real re-shoot disagreements

candidates.name: folded secondary-ridge test, PCA-grey image, doubling only
candidates.rule: double an axis if the phase-aligned mean period shape (harmonics 1-3, 8 deskewed bands, 6-period windows) has a second ridge 0.35-0.5 periods from the main one with prominence ratio r2 >= rho, and 2c <= 0.42 N; repeat at most twice
candidates.verdict: chosen with rho = 0.15: the only candidate with zero broken counts on all synthetic sets, no change on legacy13, and fewer 2x disagreements on real copies without creating any; rho 0.15-0.20 is the plateau where res / rot disagreements drop, 0.15 is the better of the two on synthetic

candidates.name: C2 + single-ridge halving (no second ridge at twice the counted period, r2h < 0.05, c/2 >= 18)
candidates.verdict: rejected: halving decisions were right 3 times and wrong 3 times on synthetic; a missing second ridge is also what alternately coloured yarns look like

candidates.name: C2 + halving gated by a significant on-axis spectral peak at half the counted frequency (whitened z >= 3)
candidates.verdict: rejected: one false halving on synthetic C, no halving on real, no consistency gain over C2

candidates.name: C2 on four images (PCA-grey and each of B, G, R pre-processed identically), max ratio
candidates.verdict: rejected: catches alternately coloured yarns (e.g. white and blue ends) in some shots but not in their re-shoots, so it creates new re-shoot 2x disagreements

candidates.name: harmonic ratio |C2| / |C1| of the folded period shape >= kappa (in addition to C2 rho 0.10)
candidates.verdict: rejected: a false doubling on legacy13 and more real resolution-copy disagreements

candidates.name: multi-estimator octave vote (lattice, profile+YIN, fft tiles, log-Gabor, fft peak; apply 2^k if >= m estimators sit within 0.15 octave of 2^k x ours)
candidates.verdict: rejected: the 2-vote version removes re-shoot disagreements but creates rotation and copy disagreements (the estimators share the octave ambiguity); the 3-vote version does nothing

candidates.name: octave-guarded fusion (keep the lattice count when the fused count is a power of two away from it)
candidates.verdict: rejected: the fusion's octave overrides are mostly right on synthetic

diagnosis_label_free: The frozen counter is mostly self-consistent on real copies: 2x disagreements on 6 / 82 re-shoot axes, 4 / 94 resolution-copy axes, 2 / 102 rotated-copy axes. Octave errors that the aggregate labels reveal must therefore be mostly SYSTEMATIC (the same fabric is read at the same octave in every shot), which no consistency signal can expose.

The lattice estimator alone is more consistent than the fused output (re-shoot 2x axes 4 vs 6): the profile/YIN and tile estimators lock onto coarse structures (colour stripes, float rows) and the fusion rule lets them override the lattice in some shots (e.g. scene group 15/38/60/61: lattice v = 141-143 in all four shots, profile v = 35-36 in all four, fused output flips with the tile vote; scenes 30/33: fused h 45 vs 90).

Visible structures behind half readings: yarns that work in pairs or floats covering two yarns (basket / oxford-like); alternately coloured yarns (white and blue ends) where the dark yarn is barely visible in the grey image; plain-weave checkerboards in yarn-dyed stripes with only two or three float rows, whose row-to-row half-period shift does not cancel; fabric rotated beyond the 15 degree candidate window.

At the frozen output the real images look like correctly counted legacy images: spectral half-shift self-similarity median -0.12 (legacy at the true count -0.18, legacy at half the true count +0.47), and the phase-aligned period shape is nearly sinusoidal (coherent |C2|/|C1| median 0.048 on the 152 representative axes; legacy13 at the true count 0.073). In most real scenes a second yarn inside the counted period is therefore not resolved as a ridge in the image, so an image-evidence rule can only correct a minority of the octave errors; octave-v1 changes 4 of the 152 axes of the 76 scene representatives.
